title: Differential latency-fence prefill/decode bin packer
creator: Priya Patel
description: Background: tail latency for short interactive requests is increasing under mixed workloads when long prefill/long-decode jobs contend with many short-turn chat requests. Current prefill/decode allocator uses coarse token-phase buckets which sometimes groups high-attention-cost prefills with low-cost decodes, causing increased queuing and jitter for latency-sensitive calls. Goal: introduce a lightweight bin-packing scheduler that creates "latency fences" around bins of work to protect short, latency-sensitive requests while still achieving good GPU utilization on throughput-heavy inputs.
proposal: Design a differential bin-packer that uses a compact cost vector per request (estimated compute cost, attention-span factor, kv-cache size, kernel-preference hint) to assign work into heterogeneous bins. Bins have a latency-fence parameter (max tolerated head-of-line delay) and packing policy (best-fit for throughput bins, bounded-fit for latency bins). Kernel selection hints from offline profiling will bias placement into bins that favor kernels with lower per-token overhead for the request shape. The allocator should operate incrementally (O(log n) per insertion) and expose telemetry for bin occupancy, miss rate for kernel hints, and fence violations.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end P99 latency for short chat requests (<= 40 tokens) improves by >= 20% relative to baseline under mixed workload synthetic test
2) End-to-end throughput for throughput-heavy batch jobs degrades by <= 8% in the same mixed workload test
3) Kernel-hint miss rate documented and <= 15% after tuning
4) New scheduler toggled by feature flag and can be rolled back without reconfiguration
5) Telemetry dashboards created: bin-occupancy, fence-violations, queue-wait-distribution, kernel-mapping-heatmap
experiment_plan: Phase A: Offline profiling to produce kernel-cost table for representative model sizes (7B, 13B, 70B) across seq lengths {16,64,256,1024}
Phase B: Implement incremental allocator in runtime with opt-in feature flag and instrumented metrics
Phase C: Canary on Dedicated pool with synthetic mixed workload (40% short chat, 60% long-prefill throughput) for 48h
Phase D: Controlled customer-facing experiment on staging teams with live traffic routing and rollback plan
perf_results_summary: Initial microbenchmarks (canary run #1) showed P99 for short chat down 18% and throughput drop ~6% on internal dedicated pool. Kernel-hint miss rate was 22% before tuning; after adding simple kernel-fallback rules it reached 12%. Observed a pathological case when many mid-length prefills (seq=256) were labelled as latency-sensitive, causing fence overprovisioning — mitigated by attention-span normalization heuristic.
decisions: Use attention-span-normalized cost instead of raw token count to estimate per-request compute
Expose kernel-hint as advisory (soft) not mandatory; runtime may fallback to compatible kernel if bin constraints require
Implement two primary bin classes: LATENCY and THROUGHPUT, and allow dynamic reclassification based on short-term SLA violations
Ship behind feature flag with metrics and automated rollback if fence-violation rate > 2% sustained over 10 minutes
